unit: Ch 10: Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Overview & Relevant Definitions
explain: An invoice is a commercial document issued by a supplier to evidence supply and enable Input Tax Credit (ITC) for the recipient.
Credit Note is issued under Section 34(1) when taxable value or tax charged exceeds actual tax payable.
Debit Note is issued under Section 34(3) when taxable value or tax charged is less than actual tax payable.
Continuous supply of goods refers to ongoing or recurrent supply under a contract with regular periodic invoicing.
Continuous supply of services means continuous service under contract for a period exceeding 3 months with periodic payment obligations.

flow.title: Document Flow in GST Supply
steps: Taxable supply occurs
Tax invoice raised by supplier
Recipient receives document
Avail ITC using valid invoice or debit note

topics.example: A telecom company providing monthly billed internet services under a 1-year contract is a continuous supply of services.
remember: A registered person cannot avail Input Tax Credit without possession of a valid tax invoice or debit note.
mistakes: Confusing continuous supply of goods (no minimum contract duration) with continuous supply of services (must exceed 3 months).

quiz.q: What is the minimum contract duration required for a service to qualify as continuous supply of services?
quiz.why: Under Section 2(33), continuous supply of services requires a contract period exceeding 3 months with periodic payment obligations.

quiz.q: Which document is issued by a supplier when the invoice value charged is found to be less than the actual value?
quiz.why: Section 34(3) states a debit note is issued when the taxable value or tax charged in an invoice is less than the actual amount payable.

topics.title: Time Limit and Manner of Issuing Tax Invoice
explain: For supply of goods involving movement, invoice must be issued on or before removal of goods.
For goods not involving movement, invoice must be issued on or before delivery or making goods available to recipient.
For services, invoice must be issued within 30 days of supply (45 days for Banks, Financial Institutions, Insurers, and NBFCs).
For continuous supply of goods, invoice is issued before/at statement date or payment receipt; for services, on/before due date, payment date, or milestone completion.
For goods sent on approval, invoice is issued on/before supply date or 6 months from removal, whichever is earlier.
Manner of issue: Goods invoice in Triplicate (Original for Recipient, Duplicate for Transporter, Triplicate for Supplier); Services in Duplicate.

flow.title: Determining Tax Invoice Time Limit
steps: Identify supply type (Goods or Services)
Check movement, completion, or approval terms
Apply specific statutory time limit
Prepare invoice in Duplicate or Triplicate

topics.example: Ritu Manufacturers dispatches goods from factory on Sept 23; the tax invoice must be issued on or before Sept 23.
remember: Insurers, banking companies, financial institutions, and NBFCs get 45 days from service completion to issue invoices.
mistakes: Assuming goods sent on approval can wait indefinitely for an invoice; the time limit is strictly capped at 6 months from removal.

quiz.q: What is the time limit for issuing a tax invoice for taxable supply of services by a normal business?
o: Within 30 days from date of supply
Within 45 days from date of supply
On or before completion of service
quiz.why: Rule 47 prescribes that a tax invoice for services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service.

quiz.q: How many copies of invoice must be prepared in case of taxable supply of goods?
quiz.why: Rule 48(1) requires invoices for supply of goods to be prepared in triplicate (Original, Duplicate, Triplicate).

topics.title: Mandatory Particulars of Tax Invoice & HSN Code Rules
explain: Tax invoice must contain supplier GSTIN, consecutive serial number (max 16 characters), date, and recipient details.
For B2C supplies of ₹50,000 or more to unregistered persons, recipient name, delivery address, and State code are mandatory.
HSN digits required: Aggregate turnover ≤ ₹5 Crore requires 4 digits for B2B (optional for B2C). Turnover > ₹5 Crore requires 6 digits for both B2B and B2C.
Invoice must explicitly show description, quantity, taxable value, tax rates, tax amounts, place of supply, and RCM applicability.
Signature or digital signature of supplier is mandatory unless generated as an e-invoice or electronically exempted.

flow.title: Structuring Tax Invoice Particulars
steps: Enter header details and unique 16-char serial number
Capture supplier and recipient GSTIN/details
Insert required HSN digits based on turnover
Break down taxable value, tax rate, and tax amount
Affix signature or e-signature

topics.example: A company with ₹8 Crore turnover in the previous FY must mention 6-digit HSN codes on all B2B and B2C tax invoices.
remember: The consecutive serial number of a tax invoice must not exceed 16 characters and must be unique for a Financial Year.
mistakes: Believing B2C invoices never require HSN codes; suppliers with aggregate turnover > ₹5 Crore must include 6-digit HSN on B2C invoices too.

quiz.q: What is the mandatory number of HSN digits for B2B supplies by a taxpayer with annual turnover exceeding ₹5 Crore?
quiz.why: Notification No. 12/2017 CT mandates 6 digits of HSN code for taxpayers with aggregate turnover > ₹5 Crore in preceding FY.

quiz.q: What is the maximum length allowed for an invoice serial number under GST?
quiz.why: Rule 46 stipulates that consecutive serial numbers must not exceed 16 characters.

topics.title: E-Invoicing System and Dynamic QR Code
topics.section: Rule 48(4), Form GST INV-1, Rule 46 (6th Proviso)
explain: E-invoicing is mandatory for registered businesses with aggregate turnover > ₹5 Crore in any preceding FY from 2017-18 onwards for B2B and export supplies.
Invoices are created on taxpayers' own accounting/ERP systems and reported to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) in JSON schema (Form GST INV-1).
IRP generates a unique 64-character Invoice Reference Number (IRN), digitally signs it, adds a QR code, and returns it.
Exempted entities: SEZ units, Insurers, Banks, NBFCs, GTAs, Passenger Transport, Multiplexes, and Government Departments/Local Authorities.
Dynamic QR Code is mandatory on B2C invoices issued by taxpayers with aggregate turnover > ₹500 Crore in any preceding FY from 2017-18.

flow.title: E-Invoice Generation Process
steps: Create invoice in billing software
Upload JSON payload to IRP
IRP generates 64-character IRN
IRP digitally signs invoice & adds QR Code
IRP auto-populates GSTR-1 & E-Way Bill

topics.example: Sharma & Associates (turnover ₹6.2 Cr) providing legal services under RCM must generate an e-invoice with IRN via IRP.
remember: SEZ units are exempt from e-invoicing, but SEZ Developers are NOT exempt if their turnover exceeds ₹5 Crore.
mistakes: Believing e-invoicing means generating invoices directly on the Government portal; it means reporting ERP-created invoices to the IRP.

quiz.q: Which of the following entities is exempt from the mandatory e-invoicing requirement?
quiz.why: Only SEZ units are exempt from e-invoicing; SEZ developers are required to issue e-invoices if their turnover exceeds the threshold.

quiz.q: What turnover threshold triggers mandatory Dynamic QR Code on B2C invoices?
quiz.why: Notification No. 14/2020 CT mandates Dynamic QR Code on B2C invoices for taxpayers with aggregate turnover exceeding ₹500 Crore.

topics.title: Revised Tax Invoice, Consolidated Invoice, & Bill of Supply
explain: Revised Tax Invoice: Issued within 1 month from registration certificate grant for supplies made during the intervening period (effective date to grant date).
Consolidated Revised Invoice: Allowed for all intra-State B2C supplies, and for inter-State B2C supplies up to ₹2,50,000 per recipient.
Small Supplies (< ₹200): Invoice not required if value < ₹200, recipient is unregistered and doesn't require invoice; daily consolidated invoice is issued at day end.
Bill of Supply: Issued by composition taxpayers or suppliers of wholly exempt goods/services; contains no tax rate or tax amount.
Invoice-cum-Bill of Supply (Rule 46A): Issued to unregistered persons when supplying both taxable and exempt goods/services together.

flow.title: Selecting Document Type
steps: Check registration status & supply nature
If Composition/Exempt -> Issue Bill of Supply
If supply value < ₹200 & B2C -> Issue Daily Consolidated Invoice
If registration granted retrospectively -> Issue Revised Invoice within 1 month

topics.example: A composition manufacturer issues a Bill of Supply mentioning 'composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies'.
remember: Multiplex cinema halls cannot avail the exemption of not issuing invoices for values under ₹200.
mistakes: Issuing a tax invoice instead of a Bill of Supply when registered under the composition scheme; composition dealers cannot collect GST.

quiz.q: Within what time period must Revised Tax Invoices be issued after grant of registration certificate?
quiz.why: Section 31(3)(a) specifies that revised tax invoices must be issued within 1 month from the date of issuance of certificate of registration.

quiz.q: Which text must prominently appear at the top of a Bill of Supply issued by a composition dealer?
o: composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies
quiz.why: Rule 49 mandates composition dealers to state 'composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies' at the top of the bill of supply.

topics.title: Vouchers: Receipt, Refund, and Payment Vouchers
explain: Receipt Voucher: Issued immediately by a registered person upon receiving advance payment for goods or services.
If tax rate or nature of supply is unknown at advance receipt: Apply 18% GST rate and treat as Inter-State supply.
Refund Voucher: Issued when advance payment is received (and Receipt Voucher issued), but no supply is subsequently made and no tax invoice is raised.
Payment Voucher: Issued by a recipient liable to pay tax under RCM (Section 9(3)/9(4)) at the time of making payment to the supplier.
RCM Invoice: Issued by a recipient liable under RCM for supplies received from an unregistered supplier within 30 days of receipt.

flow.title: Voucher Issuance Workflow
steps: Advance payment received
Issue Receipt Voucher immediately
If order cancelled & no supply made -> Issue Refund Voucher
If RCM payment made -> Issue Payment Voucher

topics.example: Om Furniture receives ₹2,00,000 advance on July 5 for a custom table; it must issue a Receipt Voucher on July 5 itself.
remember: Uncertain tax rate on advance payment defaults to 18%; uncertain nature of supply defaults to inter-State supply.
mistakes: Forgetting that a payment voucher is issued at the time of payment under RCM, whereas self-invoice for RCM from unregistered supplier is issued within 30 days of receipt.

quiz.q: If the nature of supply is not determinable at the time of receipt of advance, how should it be treated?
quiz.why: Rule 50 proviso states that if the nature of supply is not determinable at the time of advance receipt, it shall be treated as inter-State supply.

quiz.q: Which document is issued when advance money is refunded because no supply was made after receiving advance?
quiz.why: Section 31(3)(e) provides for issuing a Refund Voucher against advance payment when no supply is made and no tax invoice is issued.

topics.title: Delivery Challan & Special Transport Provisions
explain: Delivery Challan: Used to move goods without invoice in specified cases (e.g., supply of liquid gas with unknown quantity, goods sent on approval, job work, repairs, display at exhibitions).
Delivery Challan must be prepared in TRIPLICATE (Original for Consignee, Duplicate for Transporter, Triplicate for Consignor).
Goods in SKD/CKD condition or lots: Complete invoice issued before first consignment dispatch; delivery challans accompany subsequent consignments; original invoice goes with last lot.
Relaxations for Banks, Insurers, Passenger Transport, and Multiplexes: Serial numbers and recipient address are optional on their invoices/tickets.
GTA consignment note: Must state gross weight, consignor/consignee names, carriage registration number, goods details, origin, destination, and GSTIN of person paying tax.

flow.title: Transportation via Delivery Challan
steps: Goods removed for non-supply / unknown quantity
Issue Delivery Challan in Triplicate
Transport with E-Way Bill
Issue Tax Invoice upon delivery or final approval

topics.example: Ganga Industrial Gases dispatches liquid oxygen in a tanker; since exact delivered quantity varies, goods move under a Delivery Challan, and tax invoice is issued post-delivery.
remember: For SKD/CKD consignments, the complete tax invoice is issued before dispatch of the FIRST consignment, and original copy accompanies the LAST consignment.
mistakes: Thinking a delivery challan replaces a tax invoice permanently; a tax invoice must still be issued after delivery or approval of goods.

quiz.q: When goods are transported in SKD/CKD condition in lots, when must the complete tax invoice be issued?
o: Before dispatch of the first consignment
quiz.why: Rule 55(4)(a) mandates that the supplier shall issue the complete invoice before dispatch of the first consignment.

quiz.q: Which details are optional on invoices issued by banking and insurance companies?
o: GSTIN of supplier and tax rate
Serial number and address of recipient
Description of service and total value
quiz.why: Rule 54(2) relaxes the requirement of serial number and address of recipient for banking, insurance, and financial institutions.

topics.title: Credit Notes and Debit Notes
explain: Credit Note: Issued by supplier when taxable value or tax charged in invoice > actual value/tax payable, or goods are returned/deficient.
Reduction in output tax liability via Credit Note is allowed ONLY if registered recipient reverses corresponding ITC (or tax incidence isn't passed on).
Time limit to declare Credit Note in GSTR-1: On or before 30th November following the end of FY in which supply was made OR date of furnishing Annual Return, whichever is earlier.
Debit Note (Supplementary Invoice): Issued by supplier when taxable value or tax charged in invoice < actual value/tax payable.
Debit Note increases output tax liability and must be declared in GSTR-1 of the month of issue; there is no outer deadline like 30th November.

flow.title: Credit/Debit Note Determination
steps: Compare original invoice value with actual corrected value
If invoice value > actual -> Issue Credit Note
If invoice value < actual -> Issue Debit Note
Report in GSTR-1 & adjust output tax liability

topics.example: Ganesh Traders invoices 100 units at ₹1,200 instead of agreed ₹1,000; it issues a Credit Note for ₹20,000 plus GST to correct the excess tax charged.
remember: Secondary post-supply discounts not meeting Section 15(3)(b) cannot reduce GST liability; financial/commercial credit notes (without GST) are issued instead.
mistakes: Assuming there is an outer cutoff date like 30th November for issuing Debit Notes; the 30th November deadline applies strictly to Credit Notes.

quiz.q: What is the maximum time limit for declaring a Credit Note issued for a financial year in the GST return?
o: 30th November following the end of FY or date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier
quiz.why: Section 34(2) sets the deadline for declaring credit notes as 30th November following the end of the financial year or annual return filing date, whichever is earlier.

quiz.q: When a supplier mistakenly charges 5% GST instead of 18% GST on an invoice, which document should be issued?
quiz.why: Section 34(3) mandates issuing a debit note when tax charged in a tax invoice is less than the actual tax payable.

topics.title: Prohibition of Unauthorised Collection of Tax & Display of Tax
explain: Section 32 prohibits unregistered persons from collecting any GST on supplies.
Registered persons cannot collect GST except in accordance with the provisions of the CGST Act or rules thereunder (e.g., exempt supplies cannot have GST collected).
Any amount collected as 'tax' unlawfully must be deposited with the Government.
Section 33 mandates that every person liable to pay tax for a supply must prominently and separately indicate the tax amount on all tax invoices, assessment documents, and like documents.
Lumpsum billing without showing tax split separately violates Section 33 even if tax was embedded in the total price.

flow.title: Compliance for Tax Collection & Disclosure
steps: Check registration and taxability of supply
If unregistered or exempt -> Do NOT collect GST (Sec 32)
If registered and taxable -> Calculate GST
Prominently and separately display tax on invoice (Sec 33)

topics.example: Om Electronics sells a washing machine for ₹23,600; invoice must prominently show Taxable Value: ₹20,000, CGST @ 9%: ₹1,800, SGST @ 9%: ₹1,800.
remember: Section 33 makes separate, prominent disclosure of tax amount mandatory on all assessment and invoice documents.
mistakes: Believing an all-inclusive bill stating 'Total ₹47,200 (inclusive of GST)' without showing the tax breakdown complies with Section 33.

quiz.q: Can an unregistered person collect GST from customers on sales made by them?
o: Yes, if turnover is near threshold
quiz.why: Section 32 explicitly prohibits unregistered persons from collecting any amount by way of tax under GST.

quiz.q: Under Section 33, how must the tax component be shown on a tax invoice for a taxable supply?
quiz.why: Section 33 mandates that every person liable to pay tax shall prominently indicate the amount of tax separately in all invoice documents.
